stem: When coordinating post-transplant Epstein-Barr virus prevention, which intervention aligns with standard references for reducing posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) risk?

options.text: Epstein-Barr virus replication inhibitors such as ganciclovir or valganciclovir
Routine live-virus vaccination during peak immunosuppression without interval planning
Permanent discontinuation of all antiviral therapy in every recipient
No preventive measures because PTLD cannot be influenced

explanation.rationale_correct: Prevention of PTLD may include Epstein-Barr virus replication inhibitors such as antiviral drugs including ganciclovir and valganciclovir, as well as IVIG in selected cases.

rationale_incorrect.B: Live vaccines require careful timing around immunosuppression rather than routine administration during peak immunosuppression.
rationale_incorrect.C: Antiviral EBV replication inhibitors are preventive options rather than being permanently discontinued in all recipients.
rationale_incorrect.D: Preventive antiviral strategies are described for PTLD risk reduction.

stem: When monitoring a lung transplant recipient for malignancy risk, which epidemiologic pattern for posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) aligns with standard references?

options.text: PTLD is more common in nonrenal allograft recipients such as lung and heart-lung recipients
PTLD occurs only in kidney transplant recipients
PTLD incidence is identical across all organ types with no variation
PTLD never involves extranodal sites such as the gastrointestinal tract

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD is more common in nonrenal allograft recipients, likely because more intense antirejection therapy may be required; lung and heart-lung transplant types are among higher-risk groups.

rationale_incorrect.B: PTLD occurs across organ types and is particularly noted in nonrenal recipients.
rationale_incorrect.C: Incidence varies by allograft type rather than being uniform.
rationale_incorrect.D: PTLD is often extranodal and may involve the gastrointestinal tract, lung, or kidney.

stem: A pancreas-kidney recipient with diabetes mellitus is receiving antirejection therapy. Which long-term coordination priority aligns with standard post-transplant care references?

options.text: Strict control of blood glucose levels
No glucose monitoring because steroids prevent hyperglycemia
Defer all diabetes management until five years after transplant
Discontinue all immunosuppression whenever glucose is elevated

explanation.rationale_correct: Long-term post-transplant care includes strict control of blood glucose levels in patients with diabetes mellitus, particularly during periods requiring antirejection therapy.

rationale_incorrect.B: Corticosteroids and other immunosuppressants can worsen glucose control rather than preventing hyperglycemia.
rationale_incorrect.C: Glucose management is ongoing rather than deferred for years.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression changes require transplant-team guidance rather than abrupt discontinuation by the coordinator alone.

stem: A coordinator is updating post-transplant posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Epstein-Barr virus donor-seropositive to recipient-seronegative mismatch is a key PTLD risk factor.
PTLD may present with fever or lymphadenopathy.
PTLD is never treated by modifying immunosuppression.
Antiviral drugs such as ganciclovir may be used in PTLD prevention.

explanation.rationale_correct: Epstein-Barr virus mismatch, fever or lymphadenopathy, and antiviral prevention strategies are supported by standard references. Statement III is false because reduction or withdrawal of immunosuppression is a primary PTLD treatment option.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—ganciclovir-class antivirals are cited for PTLD prevention.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because immunosuppression reduction is a treatment option.
